intent: light roast - extend development time while keeping total roast time in check, resolving the astringency defect from roast-20260822-001
variable_changed: Applied previous roast's next_adjustment: color-triggered steps 215->225C at full yellow, 225->235C at full cinnamon; no reduction at FC onset; targeted drop at FC end + 150s
hypothesis: Executing the 215->225C step at full yellow and 225->235C at full cinnamon (color-triggered, on-plan rather than late) and holding through FC before dropping ~150s after FC end will extend development time to ~150s (DTR ~0.156), resolving the astringency defect from the previous roast while landing a medium-light roast around 14-15% weight loss.

sensory.aroma_drying: wet bread/grass at 2:00; no color change but sugared toast smell at 4:00
sensory.aroma_maillard: roasted peanuts at 6:00; baked bread at full yellow (8:30); sugared toast again at 10:00 turning cinnamon
sensory.aroma_development: light leaf fire smell at 15:00, not burning
sensory.color_at_yellowing: starting to turn peanut color at 5:00; full yellow at 8:30; turning cinnamon at 10:00 (looked like autumn leaves); full cinnamon at 11:00
sensory.crack_character: FC onset 17:00, very audible; FC end 18:00 (1:00 duration)
sensory.observations: Silverskin starting to flake at 12:00; really coming off by 15:00. Stepped 215->225C at full yellow (8:30, vs plan's ~7:00 target); stepped 225->235C at full cinnamon (11:00, vs plan's ~10:00 target) - both color-triggered as intended, though colors arrived later than projected. No reduction at FC onset per plan. Dropped 1:00 after FC end rather than the planned +150s, giving development time of only 60s (DTR 0.053) - well short of the 150s/0.156 target from the previous roast's next_adjustment.

cuppings.brew_method: cupping - 8g coarse ground, 150mL at 93C, 4 min steep, crust broken at 4:00
cuppings.aroma_wet: earthy, indistinct - no individual notes stood out

sweetness.notes: caramel with a bit of fruit sweetness; not hollow

cuppings.finish_quality: mild astringency, not unpleasant; some fruit character underneath
cuppings.tasting_notes_free: Tastes generically 'like coffee' - roast character more pronounced than the 8/22 cup, origin character (chocolate/strawberry) muted rather than forward. Heavy, roasty, caramel-forward. Astringency present but mild and not unpleasant, an improvement in character from the clear flaw on the previous roast, though not eliminated.
cuppings.hypothesis_result: CONTRADICTED on mechanism, though weight loss landed close to target. The plan called for color-triggered steps and a drop at FC end + 150s to reach DTR ~0.156 and resolve the astringency via extended development. In execution, both color triggers arrived later than their clock targets (full yellow at 8:30 vs ~7:00 planned; full cinnamon at 11:00 vs ~10:00 planned), driving total roast time to 19:00 - well above the normal 12-16 min band - and the drop came only 60s after FC end instead of 150s, giving DTR 0.053, the lowest yet. The extended-development mechanism was never actually tested. The milder astringency this time is more likely a byproduct of the extra total heat exposure from the long roast than of development time. Overall rating fell 8 to 7: acidity and origin character (chocolate/stone fruit/honey) dropped as roast-forward, heavier character took over.
cuppings.next_adjustment: Switch to clock-triggered steps instead of color-triggered: 215->225C at 7:00 (420s), 225->235C at 10:00 (600s), regardless of visual color state - color has run 1.5-3 min behind the clock on the last three roasts. No reduction at FC onset. Set a physical timer at FC end for +150s and drop on the timer, not by feel, to finally test the development window that's been planned twice but executed at only 60-90s both times. Goal: pull total roast time back toward the 16 min target while landing DTR in the 0.15-0.25 range. Also log ambient_temp_f this time (missing from this roast) to rule out a cooler day contributing to the slow drying/Maillard pace.
